description.narrative:
Regional Community Forestry Training Center for Asia and the Pacific (RECOFTC, Bangkok, Thailand), i samarbete med Center for International Forestry Research (CIFOR, Bogor, Indonesien), har ansökt till Sida om stöd för etablering av ett nytt regionalt forskningsnätverk för skogslandskapsförvaltning (forest landscape governance). Projektförslaget är Developing research capacity of universities in Southeast Asia on forest landscape governance: strengthening rights, reducing poverty and inequalities, and supporting sustainable development. Det nya forskningsnätverket och dess verksamhet kommer att arbeta i Sydostasien, med särskilt fokus på Kambodja, Indonesien, Laos, Myanmar, Filippinerna, Thailand och Vietnam.
Insatsen syftar till att upprätta ett sydostasiatiskt forskningsnätverk som kan genomföra inkluderande och deltagande forskning om skogslandskapsförvaltning. Dess forskningsresultat syftar till att bidra till hållbar utveckling, fattigdomsbekämpning och miljöskydd. Projektets mål och metoder betonar mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet. RECOFTC, med stöd från CIFOR och andra partners i regionen, kommer att inrätta och vara värd för ett regionalt nätverkssekretariat och en projektrådgivande kommitté, som i sin tur kommer att rekrytera forskare till forskningsnätverket. Planerade nätverksaktiviteter inkluderar nationella och regionala workshops för att samverka med ett brett spektrum av skogslandskapsaktörer och stärka forskningskapaciteten i regionen. Medel kommer at utdelas till nätverksmedlemmar för att utveckla forskningsförslag som studerar lokala, nationella och gränsöverskridande skogsförvaltningsfrågor. Nätverket kommer att samarbeta med både enskilda forskare och universitet i regionen.
Insatsens totala budget under oktober 2020 - september 2022 är 11,6 miljoner SEK. Cirka 2,2 miljoner SEK kommer at vidareförmedlas frän RECOFTC till sydostasiatiska universitet för forskningsverksamhet.

The Regional Community Forestry Training Center for Asia and the Pacific (RECOFTC, Bangkok, Thailand), in partnership with the Center for International Forestry Research (CIFOR, Bogor, Indonesia), submitted a proposal to the Embassy of Sweden in Bangkok to support the establishment of a new regional forest landscape governance research network. The project proposal is entitled "Developing research capacity of universities in Southeast Asia on forest landscape governance: strengthening rights, reducing poverty and inequalities, and supporting sustainable development". The research network and its activities will cover Southeast Asia, with a focus on Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
The intervention aims to establish a Southeast Asian research network that can carryout inclusive and participatory research on forest landscape governance that will be catalytic for sustainable development, poverty alleviation and environmental conservation. A human-rights based approach and gender equality are central to the goals and the methods of the intervention. RECOFTC, with support from CIFOR and other partners in the region, will establish and host a network Secretariat, a Project Advisory Committee, and facilitate the recruitment of researchers into the Forest Landscape Governance Research Network. Planned network activities include national and regional workshops for aligning the research network to the needs of a broad range of forest landscape stakeholders, research capacity-building, and preparatory grants for network members to develop research proposal that address local, national and transboundary forest governance issues. The Forest Landscape Governance Network will engage with individual researchers and universities in the region.
The intervention’s total budget during October 2020 - September 2022 is 11,6 million SEK. Approximately 2,2 million SEK of the intervention budget will be forwarded from organisation RECOFTC to Southeast Asian universities for research activities.

To support governments in using high quality research to improve policies and institutional frameworks for inclusive and sustainable development of forest landscapes in Southeast Asia. Specific objectives: A well-functioning regional forest landscape governance research network is established to support co-learning and co-creation of knowledge, including transboundary and multi-country research collaboration. High quality research is conducted in forest landscapes and effectively communicated to stakeholders to discuss and improve policies and institutional frameworks in supporting local communities in forest landscapes. An up to date and accessible forest governance knowledge management system is in place and tailored capacity development programs are available to support shared learning on fundamental sustainable development issues, revolving around a rights based approach, addressing poverty, gender and social inequality, in forest landscapes. Researchers have constructive and meaningful engagement with sustainable development practitioners and investors active in forest landscapes through a community of practice to support adaptation and use of findings and approaches from research; translating theory to practice.

Examples of results achieved are provided below. Examples are grouped under the overall objectives of the contribution to which they are most relevant.
1. A well-functioning inclusive regional forest landscape research network. As of 30 September 2022, the total network members were 293 persons, of which 133 are female (45 percent). Eighty-eight percent of members were from Explores focus countries (Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam). Members are mainly researchers from local and national universities, but also includes partners from civil society organizations (CSOs), government, private sector, development agencies and donors. During Phase 1, a total of 12 Program Advisory Committee (PAC) meetings were held. At the end of Phase 1, Explore Secretariat held an open vote for the PAC members in Phase 2 through Explore community of practice (CoP).
2. Stronger capacity among network members in participatory action research, rights-based approach, research proposal development, conflict mitigation, stakeholder engagement, and gender and social inclusion mechanisms. Based on the capacity development needs assessment (CDNA) and gender analysis findings, Explore Secretariat developed two trainings, seven additional workshops and two clinics to support the research team to develop research proposals. 172 network members, of which 93 female members (54%) and 79 male member enhanced and strengthened their capacity based on capacity gaps identified from Capacity Development Needs Assessment (see p. 35). The mentorship programme appears to be working well, and appreciated by both mentors and grantees. In a reflection workshop, it was noted that about 1/3 of mentors were spending more than the planned 8 working days on mentorship activities. This is interpreted as a sign of the mentors' high level of engagement for and commitment to the projects/grantees.
3. Regional, transboundary research projects mobilized on gender, climate change, environment, human rights, poverty alleviation, and covid-19 recovery. The call for proposals launched during year 1 resulted in 71 concept note submissions. Fifty-three of these met the eligibility requirements. After a rigorous scientific peer review selection process, 19 research teams were identified to receive technical and financial support to develop their research proposal. The financial support varied from US$8,340 to $18,812 with a total of US$255,343. The 19 teams include 224 researchers from 72 institutions in Southeast Asia. Most institutions are universities or research institutes, with a smaller number of NGOs and government agencies. The geographical coverage of the transboundary projects included Lao PDR (10 projects), Indonesia (10), Cambodia (5), Timor-Leste (2), Vietnam (8), Thailand (4), Philippines (2) and Myanmar (4).
4. Visibility strategy and tools developed for awareness, action, and network coordination. Explore Research Network Guidelines were developed in year 1. These guidelines supported researchers to submit concept notes that gave appropriate consideration to the principles of do no harm, and delivered on Explores objectives. The guidelines include principles of ethical research adapted from CIFOR's Research Ethics Review (RER) Policy and Toolkit covering all aspects of a research project. The guidelines prioritize the consent and use of information and anonymity of research subjects, and the inclusiveness of multi-stakeholders, especially women, ethnic and marginalized groups. Explore Secretariat actively joined various meetings to create visibility of the Explore program with the aim to share Explore's objectives and work, and to identify synergies and areas of collaboration to embed Explores work. This included events at national and regional level. Explore Secretariat continued to reach out to relevant projects, programs, networks and organizations and institutions at national, regional and global levels to extend its network and maximize synergies. Explore Secretariat established National Advisory Committee (NAC) members in Indonesia and Myanmar. In Indonesia, the NAC member meeting focused on a collaboration and synergy between Explore research proposal and Indonesias research priorities. In Myanmar, the NAC member meeting focused on risk management particularly due to military coup in February 2021. Awareness raising of the network was facilitated by 137 new media stories (5 stories, 130 social media posts and 2 blogs) and 19,554,638 social media reach and 342 engagements in the stories and blogs (see p. 37).
Unexpected results and challenges
The primary challenges encountered were the continuing COVID-19 pandemic and the deteriorating situation in Myanmar since the military coup in February 2021. To address the restrictions resulting from efforts to limit the spread of COVID-19, the Secretariat conducted nearly all of the capacity development activities online. As a result of the military coup in Myanmar, direct engagement with government organizations in the country was suspended. This had an impact on Explores ability to support researchers in Myanmar.
Explore Phase 1 was successful in achieving its objectives, and it laid a foundation for the initiation of a second phase of activities beginning in October 2022.
The success of Phase 1 can be attributed to the strength of committment by RECOFTC to the initiative, the relevance of the programmes activities (e.g. capacity building and research funding) for researchers and forest stakeholders in the region, and the active engagment of the PAC in providing guidance to the program.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
